sourceInspection.method: Pinned public GitHub raw files privately captured and SHA-256 recorded; README, license, Q&A, benchmarks, evaluation instructions and selected runtime modules inspected without execution.
sourceInspection.caveat: No DeepInfer build or benchmark was run; no checkpoint, gated datasets or internal service telemetry was obtained. Code inspection is not a correctness or security audit.
sourceInspection.publicationBoundary: Only original GhostMesh analysis, short paraphrases, pinned links and sanitized hashes are public. Full captured files remain outside Git.

custody.note: Twelve public source files, 124872 bytes in total, were retained outside Git from exact commit 774ce244; the manifest digest binds their individual hashes.

overview: DeepSeek opens an offline DeepInfer engine for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on specified accelerators; its public release omits service components and its plots use selected steady-state workloads.
whyItMatters: The source exposes useful code and methods, but draft-token throughput is not delivered user value, and the private production stack is broader than the open engine.
ghostMeshTakeaway: Inventory hardware and workload first, then compare complete services on accepted tokens, first-token and tail latency, quality, privacy, total cost and recovery.

claims.proposition: The public DeepInfer release supports offline inference for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on NVIDIA SM100 or Huawei Ascend 950.
claims.assessment: The pinned README states the scope and the tree includes runtime and build files. Source inspection confirms code presence, not working execution.
claims.limits: No installation, checkpoint execution or accelerator compatibility test was performed.
claims.sourceLocation: README: Supported models, hardware and Getting started
claims.temporalScope: DeepInfer pinned October 20, 2026 commit; external methods inspected October 21, 2026.

claims.proposition: A complete online inference service still needs KV cache, prefill/decode disaggregation and data-parallel replica load balancing not included in the public release.
claims.assessment: The maintainer explicitly lists these missing service components while the separate Q&A describes internal production infrastructure.
claims.limits: The public tree has related engine functionality; this does not prove the internal service is absent or reproduced.
claims.sourceLocation: README: Required for a complete inference service
claims.temporalScope: DeepInfer pinned October 20, 2026 commit; external methods inspected October 21, 2026.

claims.proposition: The published prefill and decode plots use four and 64 SM100 GPUs respectively under selected scale-up conditions.
claims.assessment: The README labels the GPU counts and points to the sweep script. No benchmark was run by GhostMesh.
claims.limits: No matched competitor, percentile distribution, electricity or service cost is established by these plots.
claims.temporalScope: DeepInfer pinned October 20, 2026 commit; external methods inspected October 21, 2026.

claims.proposition: The documented decode throughput calculation credits all draft tokens under full acceptance regardless of actual acceptance.
claims.assessment: The benchmark documentation gives the formula and the plotting method allows an assumed acceptance fraction.
claims.limits: An acceptance-adjusted curve is still a modeled output, not measured end-to-end useful tokens or user quality.
claims.sourceLocation: examples/README.md: Stage decoupling and metrics; Sweeps
claims.temporalScope: DeepInfer pinned October 20, 2026 commit; external methods inspected October 21, 2026.

claims.proposition: The default benchmark uses a shared cached prefix with 32,768-token context, 4,096 uncached tokens, 64 decode requests and nextn five.
claims.assessment: The pinned examples documentation sets these defaults and explains decoupled prefill and decode scheduling.
claims.limits: Different tenant, cold-cache, burst and long-tail workloads may change the observed result.
claims.sourceLocation: examples/README.md: Benchmark defaults and shared prefix
claims.temporalScope: DeepInfer pinned October 20, 2026 commit; external methods inspected October 21, 2026.

claims.proposition: DeepSeek reports reference Pass@1 figures of 99.9% AIME 2026, 93.4% GPQA Diamond and 42.6% HLE-Full for its default V4.1 configuration.
claims.assessment: The eval README gives sample counts, scoring method and those reference figures. The pinned capture lacks an independent completed output bundle.
claims.limits: Datasets are sourced separately, some gated, and default scoring needs a judge service; no quality/speed joint run was performed.
claims.sourceLocation: eval/README.md: Reference results, data preparation and scoring
claims.temporalScope: DeepInfer pinned October 20, 2026 commit; external methods inspected October 21, 2026.

claims.proposition: DeepSeek describes larger internal E/P/D, KV and replica services, cluster token volume and a revenue-per-GPU-hour illustration.
claims.assessment: The deployment Q&A is an operator account of a broader private serving system, distinct from the released offline engine.
claims.limits: No independent traffic telemetry, cost accounting or profit evidence is available in the inspected source.
claims.temporalScope: DeepInfer pinned October 20, 2026 commit; external methods inspected October 21, 2026.

claims.proposition: An online service comparison should include queueing, time to first token, inter-token delay, tail latency and quality under the same workload.
claims.assessment: GhostMesh derives this test from the limits of offline charts and primary SGLang and vLLM benchmark guidance.
claims.limits: The comparison is proposed, not executed; alternative documentation does not establish performance superiority.
claims.sourceLocation: GhostMesh experiment; SGLang and vLLM serving benchmark documentation
claims.temporalScope: DeepInfer pinned October 20, 2026 commit; external methods inspected October 21, 2026.

claims.proposition: DeepInfer adoption on Hyperion requires a verified hardware, model, data and service-control inventory before any installation or deployment recommendation.
claims.assessment: This is GhostMesh’s bounded engineering recommendation based on the narrow supported-hardware list and missing service components.
claims.limits: The actual Hyperion accelerator inventory and workload were not verified here; no Hyperion or Qwen action was performed.
claims.sourceLocation: README: Supported hardware; Required for a complete inference service

relationships.reason: Both Readers challenge a jump from reported model-system speed to a product decision. The earlier analysis concerns parallel-agent performance and outcome evaluation; DeepInfer concerns inference throughput, accepted tokens and service latency. Neither source independently verifies the other.

Both Readers test the gap between owning compute and controlling a usable private service. The earlier reading examines local versus cloud trust and cost; this one identifies KV, egress, routing and recovery boundaries for inference. This is an architectural reading route, not corroboration of DeepSeek metrics.

Both Readers separate raw accelerator or engine throughput from useful service output. The operator analysis asks how serving software, latency and full cost change the buyer result; DeepInfer publishes an offline engine, not the surrounding service. These distinct sources do not corroborate each other’s performance claims.

normalization.relationshipDisposition: Three qualified editorial routes connect performance-to-product interpretation, local control boundaries and service economics. They do not corroborate DeepSeek benchmark or production metrics.

relationshipReview.rationale: Compared the pinned DeepInfer source with all 32 existing Readers. Three specific routes link performance-to-product interpretation, local service-control boundaries and inference service economics. Other topic overlap does not establish independent corroboration or a shared empirical result. The later HORTRAME film was also compared; its visual swarm and mathematical references do not establish a further serving relationship.
